title: Replying to @mhairiledgerwood Fringe Show 19: My Mother’s Funeral ⭐️⭐...
transcript: One of the reasons I even went back to go to the fringe for another three days was to see shows like My Mother's Funeral that everybody was raving about and I had to go see for myself. And it did not disappoint. My Mother's Funeral is a new play by Kelly Jones, all about playwright Abigail, whose mother dies, and she all of a sudden faces the fact that she has to pay for the funeral. And funerals are freaking expensive. And Abigail is very much a working class playwright. She was just denied commission for a play that she had been working on because the people who commissioned it were like, this is not what our audiences want. And so, in a desperate plea, she decides to write about her mother, and thus, my mother's funeral. And this play has so many layers and is so meta, which I freaking love, especially the exploration of, like, what is real and what do we fictionalize for art, and how much of ourselves do we put into our art? Like, is this play that we are watching the play that the playwright had to write in order to pay for her mother's funeral, or is that all fictionalized? How much is real? How much is true? How much of that actually matters? How much of yourself do you lose for the sake of the audience? Right? Like, how much do you have to fictionalize in order to cater to an Audience. And how much do you want to cater to an audience? And on top of all the really cool meta layers to this play, you also have a look at, like, the working class artist dilemma of, like, you don't know where your next paycheck is coming from. How do you do things like pay for a funeral? And what does it mean to be buried with dignity? So many fantastic aspects of this play. What Kelly Jones has written here is just, ah, it is a fantastic work of art on so many different levels, and it is beautifully performed by this entire cast, especially Nicole Sawyer as Abigail, the playwright. She is just so good and sucks you in right away. And Deborah Baker and Samuel Arnfield are incredible in this, playing multiple characters throughout that she interacts, including the titular mother and her brother. And they also play a multitude of other characters, including, you know, bank lenders, people at the hospital that are trying to get Abigail to come pick up her mother's body, but she can't afford to. The funeral directors. The artistic director who's commissioning her play. Like, there's so many different characters beautifully portrayed by, uh, just a cast of three, and just beautifully directed by Charlotte Bennett. And just the use of space in the round. But also there was a scenic moment near the end that just made me cry. I love a good scenic moment. Anyway, I love multi Layered pieces of theater. I love when theater gets meta, and I love when a show sticks the landing, and this one absolutely, as I hope my mother's funeral has a huge long life after the Fringe Festival, it is doing essentially a UK tour, so it's playing in multiple cities across the UK. So if you are there anytime between now and the middle of October at take a look to see if this is playing in an area near you. And keep an eye out for this play in the future, because I definitely think that we are going to see more from it. It is just. It's such a well written piece of theater, and I definitely want to see more in the future from playwright Kelly Jones because this was so exquisitely put together. Also, thank you for requesting this review. I do have a lot of reviews to get through from my great theater adventure, so if there's one that I have not talked about yet and you want to to see me talk about it sooner, definitely request it in a comment and I will get to it sooner rather than later. And all of my reviews are spread across multiple playlists depending on the city that I saw them in, so definitely check that out.
